title: The Ultimate 50th Celebration Board
seo_title: 50th Birthday Charcuterie Board for 20–30: Ultimate Plan
description: The ultimate 50th celebration charcuterie board for 20–30: seven cheeses, jamón ibérico and six more meats, truffle honey, figs and gold leaf. The book's finale.
hook: The finale of the first book: the best of everything, for a 50th birthday or any milestone worth celebrating.
why: Seven cheeses covering every texture, from buttery Brillat-Savarin and pungent Époisses to 24-month Comté, truffle pecorino and Parmigiano-Reggiano. The rule isn't the most expensive version of everything, it's the best version of each.

Jamón ibérico, 24-month prosciutto and speck lead the meats, and truffle honey, aged balsamic, quince and honeycomb give each cheese its partner. Gold leaf is optional, but this is the board that earns it.

timeline.what: Shop the cheese counter; cut the hard cheeses and wrap them.
Take out the hard cheeses; set out the boards and bowls.
Take out the soft cheeses; place all eight.
Add the meats, fruit and breads.
Add the gold leaf and truffle honey; raise a glass.

faq.q: What do you serve at a 50th birthday party?
faq.a: A grand charcuterie table is ideal: it feeds a crowd, looks spectacular and works for a cocktail party or as the main food.
About $175 to $300 for 20 to 30 people, depending on the cheeses and the jamón.
Yes. Halve every quantity and use four or five cheeses and four meats for 10 to 15 people.
